subject: arts-music
unit_title: Cultural Ownership, Ethics, and the Economics of Practice
essential_question: Whose story is this to tell, and what does telling it well require?
standards: Michigan Arts Education Standards: Visual Arts — Connecting
project_brief: Research and present an ethics case study on artistic practice, in writing or in a chosen private or shared format, with sourced evidence and a defended position. This is the grade 10 culminating project for "Cultural Ownership, Ethics, and the Economics of Practice" (ma-g10-arts-and-music-u05, unit 5), built around cultural ownership and collaborative practice, appropriation appreciation and documented attribution, censorship access and public funding of the arts, artist rights contracts and fair compensation, and representation audience and social impact. Research and present an ethics case study on artistic practice, in writing or in a chosen private or shared format, with sourced evidence and a defended position. Working with cultural ownership and collaborative practice, appropriation appreciation and documented attribution, censorship access and public funding of the arts, and artist rights contracts and fair compensation, choose a private, small-audience, or public sharing format — none is required over another, and a written or no-audio alternative is always acceptable.
requirements: Address every topic listed for this unit: cultural ownership and collaborative practice, appropriation appreciation and documented attribution, censorship access and public funding of the arts, artist rights contracts and fair compensation, representation audience and social impact, and ethical sourcing and sustainable materials.

Meet the performance task as written: Research and present an ethics case study on artistic practice, in writing or in a chosen private or shared format, with sourced evidence and a defended position.
Show your work or process, not just a final result — a process note, sketch log, commit history, or draft trail.
Complete the checklist in this package before submitting.
primary_task: Research and present an ethics case study on artistic practice, in writing or in a chosen private or shared format, with sourced evidence and a defended position. Working with cultural ownership and collaborative practice, appropriation appreciation and documented attribution, censorship access and public funding of the arts, and artist rights contracts and fair compensation, choose a private, small-audience, or public sharing format — none is required over another, and a written or no-audio alternative is always acceptable.
critique_criteria: A named viewer, listener, or reader can point to a specific choice in the work and connect it back to cultural ownership and collaborative practice or another named topic from this unit.
The piece shows at least one deliberate revision — a version-two decision made because the first attempt did not achieve the intended effect.
The student can explain the intended effect on an audience in their own words, separate from just describing what was made.
Only the student's own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt appears in the piece — no unlicensed lyrics, sheet music, or protected work is reproduced.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: Sharing this project publicly is always optional and never required for full credit. You may present live to a small audience of your choosing, present privately to just your facilitator, submit a recording made only for your own review, or submit a written/described account of the finished work instead.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: If any part of this task could involve singing, speaking on camera, or being recorded, you may instead notate the piece, write a detailed description or script, use body percussion or an instrument in place of your voice, or perform live for your facilitator with no recording made at all. No lesson in this unit requires a voice recording, a camera, or a photo.

copyright_and_authorship: The final submitted work must remain your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI assistant may help you plan, explain a concept, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but may not produce the graded work itself. Use only your own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt — never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or another protected work without the rights to do so.
remediation: If the piece isn't coming together, return to a single, smaller exercise focused only on cultural ownership and collaborative practice, revisit one worked example or model from this unit, and rebuild your confidence with that one element before returning to the full project.
extension: Once the core piece is finished, create a second short variation that explores appropriation appreciation and documented attribution from a different angle, or write a short artist's statement comparing your original intent with what the finished work actually communicates.
